html:
A great earthquake of magnitude about 8 that struck northern Bihar in India and Nepal on 15 January 1934. More than ten thousand people died.

The shaking turned soft ground in the Ganges plain to liquid, so whole towns sank and broke apart. Munger and Muzaffarpur were almost entirely destroyed. In the Kathmandu valley, many temples and houses in Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur fell, and Nepal's Rana government led rebuilding there.

The quake also caused a famous argument. Gandhi said it was divine punishment for the sin of untouchability. Rabindranath Tagore publicly rebuked him, saying that linking a physical disaster to moral failings was superstition, and that such logic would blame the victims. The debate is still cited on science, faith and reform.

The Himalayan front, where India pushes under Asia, has produced many such quakes, including the Assam earthquake of 1950 and the Nepal earthquake of 2015.
sum: A great earthquake of magnitude about 8 that struck northern Bihar in India and Nepal on 15 January 1934. More than ten thousand people died.
